stormAlert.headline: Get to shore now!
stormAlert.body: A level 2 storm warning is in effect near {{spotName}} — staying on the water with a SUP is forbidden and life-threatening.

steps.1: Paddle to the nearest shore — not necessarily back to your starting point if that is farther away.
steps.2: If you cannot reach the shore: kneel down, reduce your wind profile, keep your ankle leash on.
steps.3: If you are in trouble, call water rescue: +36 30 383 8383.

floodAlert.headline: Get ashore immediately!
floodAlert.body: A level III flood alert is in effect near {{spotName}} — being on the flooded river with a SUP is forbidden and life-threatening.

steps.1: Paddle to the nearest safe bank right away — you will not be able to paddle back against a flooding river.
steps.2: Stay clear of overhanging trees, bridges and floating debris: the current pushes you into them and the board can flip underneath.
steps.3: If you are in trouble, call water rescue: +36 30 383 8383.

list.title: Basic info
list.lead: What's allowed, what isn't, and what to watch for — navigation rules, safety notes and practical info for the four most popular Hungarian waters. This isn't playful trivia — it's what you need to know before you launch.

detail.lastVerified: Last verified: 2026-08-13. Rules change from time to time — if in doubt, check the current notice from the local authority or operator.
detail.relatedLeash: Leash — what it's for and which type you need
detail.relatedPfd: Life vest — when you can't skip it

level1.signal: about 45 flashes/minute · gusts of 40–60 km/h expected, signals at least 30 minutes before the wind arrives
level1.action: stay within 500 m of the shore

level2.action: launching and staying on the water is strictly forbidden

legalBasis.0: Act XLII of 2000, Section 87 § point 43 — on water transport
legalBasis.2: Decree 46/2001 (XII. 27.) BM — basic rules for being on open water

balaton.title: Lake Balaton
balaton.tag: Classified as bathing equipment · storm warning system active

rules.0: On Lake Balaton, a SUP is legally classified as "bathing equipment" — it may only be used where swimming is also permitted.
rules.1: As a result, wearing a life vest is not a legal requirement here — the rule differs on the Danube, the Tisza and Lake Tisza, where a life vest or safety ankle leash is mandatory (see below). Wearing one is still strongly recommended here too.
rules.2: Distance from shore: up to 1000 m on the Somogy (southern) shore, up to 500 m on the Veszprém/Zala (northern) shore — which means the lake cannot be crossed at the Tihany strait.
rules.3: Launching is forbidden in shipping lanes, near harbours and docks, near navigation buoys, in designated windsurfing, kayaking and wakeboarding zones, near bridges (e.g. the Tihany strait), anywhere marked with a prohibition sign, and in protected nature areas.
rules.4: Wearing a life vest is always mandatory for anyone under 14 and for non-swimmers.

balaton.safetyIntro: Lake Balaton's storm warning system runs from April to October — flashing yellow signals at fixed shore stations and on mobile beach lamps.

safetyNotes.0: Lake Balaton is known for storms that form very quickly — this is the single most important safety message for this lake.
safetyNotes.1: Water rescue hotline: 1817, general emergency number: 112.

practical.0: The storm warning system only operates between April 1 and October 31 — outside that window there is no light-signal warning at all, so pay extra attention on your own.
practical.1: Check out our Lake Balaton spots for current wind and water data.

tisza-to.title: Lake Tisza
tisza-to.tag: Kisköre reservoir · classified as water sports equipment

rules.0: Here a SUP is legally classified as "water sports equipment" — unlike Lake Balaton and Lake Velence. For a swimmer aged 14 or over doing normal paddling, wearing a life vest OR a safety ankle leash is enough; the local operator (SUP Bázis) cites this directly, with a precise legal reference.
rules.1: Wearing a life vest is always mandatory for anyone under 14, for non-swimmers, and for everyone while fishing or using a boat hook.
rules.2: Distance from shore without escort: up to 500 m.
rules.3: Motor-restricted nature reserve zones — Porong-tava, Ispán-tava, Hód, Gaznyilas, Partos-fenék, Óhalászi-holtág — allow paddling/SUP and electric motors but not combustion engines: these are, somewhat counterintuitively, the quieter, calmer stretches for paddlers, not no-go zones.
rules.4: Southwest of route 33, combustion engines are capped at 4 kW.
rules.5: Right of way on the water: large vessels first, then sailboats, then paddlers/SUP, and only then motorboats — motorised rental boats must give way to paddlers.

tisza-to.safetyIntro: The same storm warning system operates here as on Lake Balaton.

safetyNotes.0: The table below uses the same level logic as Lake Balaton.
safetyNotes.1: If you're unsure about local wind conditions, ask the shore operators — they know the day-to-day situation best.

practical.0: Main launch points: Poroszló (Albatrosz Harbour) and Tiszafüred.
practical.1: Local rental/instruction operators (e.g. SUP Bázis in Poroszló) can give you a fresh, local briefing before you launch.

duna.title: Danube
duna.tag: Budapest stretch · classified as water sports equipment

rules.0: Here a SUP is legally classified as "water sports equipment" — wearing a life vest or safety ankle leash is mandatory, and the water police enforce it.
rules.1: Staying inside the marked shipping lane (between red and green buoys) is forbidden; if you need to cross it, do so as quickly as possible.
rules.2: A 100 m exclusion zone applies around navigation buoys, large vessels and floating work equipment.
rules.3: A 300 m exclusion zone applies around locks and hydraulic structures; 100 m around bridges, water intakes and ferry crossings.
rules.4: Night paddling is forbidden; so is staying in ports, mooring areas, and designated water-ski/jet-ski lanes.
rules.5: Group or organised SUP events need prior coordination with the navigation authority — a formal navigation closure has already been issued for one such event on the Budapest stretch.
rules.6: During icy periods the authority can impose a full navigation ban on small craft and water sports equipment — always check current notices in winter.

safetyNotes.0: Expect commercial ship traffic and wake, strong eddies and suction near hydraulic structures, hypothermia risk, and drowning risk at night or in poor visibility.
safetyNotes.1: The Danube's current can be significant even on stretches that look calm — if you're unsure, stay close to shore and avoid the main channel.

practical.0: Known Budapest launch points: Római-part (Béke boathouse), Csepel (Kolonics György Water Sports Centre), the Ráckeve branch of the Danube (BEAC), the Pesterzsébet SUP base, and local rental operators around Szentendre and Göd.
practical.1: Check out our Budapest spots for current water conditions.

tisza.title: Tisza river
tisza.tag: River · water level is the main safety factor

rules.0: A SUP is presumably classified as "water sports equipment" here too, as on the Danube — we couldn't find a Tisza-specific legal citation, but the same life-vest-or-leash rule is likely under the general framework of the Navigation Regulations. Ask local tour operators if you're unsure.
rules.1: On some river sections, commercial tour operators ask for a registration form before you set off — that's operator policy, not a legal requirement.

safetyNotes.0: Water level is the main danger here: at low water, exposed rocks and gravel bars are a hazard; at high water, the current runs well above normal and low banks can become impossible to land on safely. Always check the current water level before you go.
safetyNotes.1: Never attempt to cross a weir or dam without using the marked lock or bypass channel — doing so can be fatal. Only the marked lock/channel is safe for kayaks, canoes and SUPs (e.g. at the Kisköre and Tiszalök dams).
safetyNotes.2: On the upper Tisza, near Visó, there's also a submerged-rock hazard — this mostly matters for multi-day kayak/canoe tours rather than local SUP paddling.
safetyNotes.3: If you're unsure about the water level, ask local tour operators or check the live water level forecast (see below).

practical.0: A popular section for beginners and intermediates: Tiszabecs → Szatmárcseke on the upper river — a comfortable pace is around 15–25 km/day.
practical.1: Live water level forecast: eveznijo.hu's "Vízállás előrejelzés" — check it before you go.
practical.2: Backwaters — the oxbow lakes along the river — offer calmer, more predictable water than the Tisza's main channel, a good choice for beginners or a calmer day.
